title: Dave Canales: 'The energy was right' coming out of the bye week
headline: Panthers' returning trio (Moton, Wharton, Etienne) looked good in padded practice but none is cleared yet; Jalen Coker looked great but is limited coming off a quad and ankle issue, with the full injury report due Thursday.
summary: Canales called the first post-bye padded practice spirited and high-energy, with the team looking fresh and the returning players clearly excited to be back on the field. He said Taylor Moton, Tershawn Wharton and Trevor Etienne all got significant reps and looked good, but he will not decide on their Sunday status until he sees how their bodies respond to the physical session, with the full injury report coming tomorrow. He explained the schedule: a light Monday with meetings, a padded Tuesday to knock off rust, a recovery day Wednesday, and a high-mileage Thursday. A player who was placed on IR had a shoulder surgery that will be season-ending, while his knee issue is non-surgical rehab, and he will stay connected to the team. On rookie Zakee Wheatley, Canales said he has been a strong open-field tackler and has magnificent hands, with the next step being converting chances downfield. He praised Bryce Young's RPO execution against Detroit, explaining that the concept works when linebackers and nickels must choose between run fits and route coverage, and said Chuba Hubbard's downhill running fits that concept. On Darren Waller, Canales said he is pleased with his production, which has created horizontal and vertical stretch and favorable matchups, but there is still more to unlock. He also said front-office talks about roster moves happen constantly, and he is focused on Philadelphia.

title: HC Sean Payton on Broncos’ crowd noise: ‘It’s been fantastic’
headline: Payton says Bo Nix must balance aggression with lower-risk throws, a watch item for his fantasy outlook against Seattle
summary: Payton said the short week is being handled with walk-through reps on what the team has already practiced, and he noted that playing at home helps. He called Seattle's defense complete in every statistical area, with a strong front, excellent coverage fits, good run defense, and a effective pressure package under coordinator Mike Macdonald. On quarterback play, he said Bo Nix and he are constantly working to make throws less risky through earlier progressions and first or second reads, while avoiding falling so far behind that the game forces a different style. He said the running game had more consistency in the last game, though rhythm depends on getting enough touches. He framed the defense's turnover success as purposeful coaching, citing late-game punch-outs and momentum swings. On end-of-game situations, he said the staff reviews league-wide examples each week and keeps reminding play-callers of clock and timeout scenarios. Asked about the crowd, he said the atmosphere has been fantastic and the team has stopped using crowd-noise tactics. He also acknowledged that Seattle's pressure looks on third down are a real issue that the team has to solve.

signals.claim: Nix will be steered toward quicker, lower-risk progression throws, with more aggression only when the game situation calls for it.
signals.note: A shift toward safer throws could limit explosive plays and passing-yardage upside, but it also suggests a more stable floor.
signals.quote: we're constantly grinding to come to calm it down

title: Sean McVay & Matthew Stafford speak on the Rams’ 37-34 Week 5 overtime loss to the Bills
headline: McVay says he regrets the third-and-five call and the kick instead of going for it, and no injuries were discussed in the 37-34 OT loss to Buffalo.
summary: McVay said he was proud of the group's battle on both sides of the ball and in coverage units, but the kicking game, especially a PAT that wasn't close to good enough, cost the Rams the game. He took responsibility for the third-and-five play call, saying he wished he had called a better play and gone for it on third down instead of kicking. He said he would evaluate everything and review film on the penalties and pre-snap mistakes, which he said were a focus this week, though he didn't have a clear answer on why they persisted. He acknowledged the early kick coverage was poor but said the group fixed it afterward. McVay said he was very upset, said the team can't let this loss beat them twice, and said the team needs to regroup and reset. He ruled out going for two after the late touchdown.

topics.detail: McVay blamed himself for the third-and-five call and the decision to kick the PAT rather than go for it, and said he would evaluate everything.
McVay said he needed to review the penalties and pre-snap issues and admitted he had no clear explanation, a recurring problem he said he can do better at helping players clean up.
McVay said the opening kick coverage was not good, but it was fixed, and there were some positives from the coverage unit.

Stafford said the final drive was about getting close for a field goal or making a play on a run, and that the team wanted to be smart with the ball. Stafford also said the team didn't use a timeout on the goal-line play, instead trusting the players to run the play quickly.
Stafford, not McVay, praised Puka Nacua after a question about his 17 catches, saying he can access all areas of the field and is strong in the screen game and on the perimeter.
